NFA Tree Lab

How it works

PDA mode: select “PDA — with a stack” to load the 1001 exercise. Every tree node shows its stack (top on the left). Arrows in the state diagram use input, pop → push.

State diagram: shows every state and transition, independently of a string. The incoming arrow marks the start; double circles mark accepting states.

Computation tree: each row consumes one input symbol, shown under “Symbol read.” Nodes show state names.

ε-moves consume nothing. Each ε-move has its own labeled arrow between states on the same row, including before the first symbol or after the last.

Double circles mark accepting configurations after all input is consumed. You may stop there even if an ε-move is also available. Bold paths lead to these endpoints.

Click a node to see its path, including every individual ε-move. Branches stop when no next symbol can be consumed.

Your NFA

Use letters or symbols such as a, b, x, α, #, or $. Each input symbol is one character; ε means no input.

Add a transition

Symbol buttons insert into the transition field you last selected.

One arrow per line: from, symbol, to

Use eps for ε. List each choice separately.

Start with an empty stack. Each transition reads input, pops a matching top symbol, then pushes a symbol. Use eps to skip any operation. Stack top is on the left. Accept by final state after all input is read.

Leave blank for the empty string. Do not type ε into the input string.
